overview: Born Jorge Mario Bergoglio in Buenos Aires to a family of Italian immigrants, Pope Francis led the Catholic Church from 2013 to 2025 as the first Jesuit pope, the first Latin American pontiff, and the first born outside Europe since the eighth century. He shifted the papacy's tone toward pastoral simplicity and the global margins—championing the poor, migrants, interfaith dialogue, and environmental protection while giving laypeople and women new roles in Vatican governance—a course that drew spirited debate from both traditionalists and reformers. Over twelve years he tilted the College of Cardinals away from Europe, helped broker diplomatic openings such as the US–Cuba thaw, and died on Easter Monday 2025 the morning after offering his final blessing in St. Peter's Square.

keyMoments.title: Buenos Aires's Slum Bishop
keyMoments.text: When Jorge Mario Bergoglio took over the archdiocese of Argentina's capital in 1998, he sold off its bank shares to pull it back from near-bankruptcy and doubled the number of priests working in the city's shantytowns. Regularly visiting the impoverished neighborhoods himself, he became known locally as the **villero bishop**, or slum bishop. Even after **Pope John Paul II** made him a cardinal in 2001, Bergoglio turned down the ornate episcopal palace for a small apartment, where he cooked his own meals and rode public transit across the city.

keyMoments.title: First Pope from the Americas
keyMoments.text: Following **Pope Benedict XVI**'s resignation, cardinals in the **2013 papal conclave** elected Bergoglio on the fifth ballot, making him the first **Jesuit** pontiff and the first born outside Europe since the eighth century. After Brazilian Cardinal Cláudio Hummes embraced him and whispered, "Don't forget the poor," Bergoglio chose the name **Francis** in honor of Francis of Assisi and stepped onto St. Peter's balcony in a plain white cassock without the traditional red, ermine-trimmed cape. He greeted the crowd with a casual "Good evening," moved into the **Domus Sanctae Marthae** guesthouse instead of the Apostolic Palace, and rode back from his election in a minivan with the other cardinals before stopping by his pre-conclave residence to collect his bags and pay his own bill.

keyMoments.title: Care for Our Common Home
keyMoments.text: In 2015, Francis issued **Laudato si'**, an encyclical taking its title—"Praise be to you"—from **Saint Francis of Assisi**'s canticle celebrating nature as Mother Earth. Rather than addressing Catholics alone, he wrote explicitly to **every person living on this planet**, drawing on scientific research and Orthodox **Patriarch Bartholomew** to confront climate degradation, unchecked consumption, and what he called a throwaway culture. Refusing to treat ecology and poverty as separate crises, he framed environmental ruin as a moral wound falling hardest on the vulnerable, calling the plundered earth itself among the most abandoned and maltreated of the poor.

keyMoments.title: A Less European Conclave
keyMoments.text: By the time Francis died on **21 April 2025**, his twelve years of appointments had reshaped the **College of Cardinals** that would choose his successor. Cardinals he elevated made up **80 percent** of the 135 voting-age electors, shrinking Europe's share from 51 percent in 2013 to 40 percent while lifting the Asia-Pacific region from 10 to 18 percent and sub-Saharan Africa from 8 to 12 percent. Even though Europe remained overrepresented relative to its share of the world's Catholics, Francis had decisively tilted the church's highest electoral body away from its historic European base.

deepFacts.text: Before entering the seminary, young Jorge Bergoglio worked as a bouncer and a janitor, then earned a chemical technician's diploma and tested food in a Buenos Aires laboratory. At age 21, a life-threatening bout of pneumonia and three cysts forced surgeons to remove part of one lung—an old wound that contributed to the chronic lung damage behind the winter respiratory infections of his final years.

Hours after war erupted in Gaza in October 2023, Francis placed a phone call to Holy Family Church, the Gaza Strip's only Catholic parish, starting a nightly routine that lasted a year and a half. He refused to speak solely with the parish priest, insisting on greeting everyone crowded into the room with the reassurance, "I am with you, don't be afraid," and made his final call on Holy Saturday night, less than two days before his death.

In June 2022, nearly three years before his death, Francis signed a spare spiritual testament devoted to a single subject: his grave. He asked to lie in an unornamented floor niche inside Rome's Basilica of Saint Mary Major, the Marian sanctuary where he stopped to pray at the beginning and end of every foreign journey. The stone was to bear only one word—"Franciscus"—and he had already arranged for a private benefactor to cover the burial costs.

connections.reason: His 2013 resignation triggered the conclave that elected Francis, who then lived alongside him in the Vatican as pope emeritus until Benedict's death in 2022.
Bergoglio took his papal name in honor of the medieval friar's devotion to poverty, peace, and creation, later drawing the title of his climate encyclical Laudato si' from the saint's canticle.
He elevated Bergoglio to cardinal in 2001, and Francis canonized him alongside John XXIII in 2014.
Founder of the Society of Jesus, the religious order Bergoglio entered in 1958 before becoming the first Jesuit pope.
Elevated to cardinal by Francis in 2023, Robert Francis Prevost was elected in May 2025 as his successor and the second pope from the Americas.

As Argentina's Jesuit provincial superior during the 1970s military dictatorship, Bergoglio faced lasting scrutiny over the 1976 abduction of two Jesuit priests while others credited him with secretly helping dissidents escape.
At Obama's request in 2014, Francis acted as a behind-the-scenes mediator in the talks that restored full diplomatic relations between the United States and Cuba.
Francis helped broker the 2014 US–Cuba diplomatic thaw with Castro's government and met the Cuban leader in 2015, after which Castro publicly mused about returning to the Catholic Church.
During Italy's March 2020 lockdown, Francis delivered an extraordinary Urbi et Orbi blessing in St. Peter's Square and created a Vatican commission to respond to the pandemic's social fallout.

From October 2023 until the night before his final Easter, Francis phoned Gaza's sole Catholic parish every evening and used his last public appearance to call for a ceasefire and the release of hostages.
